name: South Africa

income_tax.summary: 2026/27 resident tax runs from 18% to a 45% top rate above ZAR 1,878,600, with the primary rebate of ZAR 17,820 folded into the brackets as a 0% band to the ZAR 99,000 tax threshold (under age 65). The only employee levy is UIF at 1% up to ZAR 212,544 a year; the self-employed pay no equivalent social security. The Remote Work Visa requires gross annual income of about ZAR 650,796.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: No social security levy for self-employed persons (PwC: no comprehensive social security system). Employer-only Skills Development Levy of 1% is not counted.
income_tax.local_tax_note: The primary rebate (ZAR 17,820, SARS 2026/27) is folded into the brackets exactly as a 0% band up to the ZAR 99,000 threshold (18% x 99,000 = 17,820); the brackets above are SARS's. Secondary/tertiary rebates and medical scheme credits are not applied. Tax year 1 March 2026 to 28 February 2027.

regimes.name: Remote Work Visitor's Visa (s11(1)(b)(iv))
regimes.description: Visa for people employed by or contracting with a foreign employer or clients, effective 9 October 2024; local employment is not allowed and status cannot be changed inside the country. Holders are taxed at normal South African rates once tax resident; SARS registration is needed after 183 days in a 12-month period (treaty residents) or on arrival otherwise, and may apply regardless of a tax treaty.
regimes.duration_note: Valid up to 36 months, reported not renewable (WhereNext).

residence_routes: EU, US and other citizens: visa-free entry varies by passport, but the Remote Work Visitor's Visa lets a remote worker for a foreign employer stay more than three months and up to three years (reported minimum gross income ZAR 650,796). It does not lead to permanent residence. Skilled employees need a general work visa or critical skills visa tied to a South African employer; those rules were not researched here.
